note_on_timing: src/train/api.py CHANGED mid-audit (md5 6e3be2e7c0b97aefeebbab2b938df9f2). The two defects I first measured -- Windows(0) firing every check, and the per-flush rate deficit -- have both been repaired in the file since. Everything below is re-measured against the CURRENT body.

findings.claim: due()'s headline sentence, 'True at most once per period WINDOWS elapsed since this key last fired', is measurably false under the new floor-division catch-up. Two fires can land one window apart on a 100-window period.
findings.failure: Gate declared Windows(100), evaluated every window except a 1000-window blackout (windows 500..1499). Fire steps: [101,201,301,401,1500,1501,1601,...]. Gap 1500->1501 = 1 window. The seed advances by 10 whole periods to 1401, leaving remainder 99, so the very next window satisfies elapsed>=100. Bounded: exactly one short gap per blackout, then back on a clean lattice.

findings.claim: The comment 'THE FLOOR-DIVISION IS WHAT KEEPS IT FROM BURSTING ... so exactly one fire happens per call' does not hold in the sense it means: the gate does fire on two consecutive calls after a gap.
findings.failure: same run as above: fires at window 1500 and again at window 1501, consecutive evaluations, declared period 100.

findings.claim: Per-flush evaluation now matches the per-window RATE exactly, but individual gaps are routinely shorter than the declared period -- the spacing guarantee the pre-fix rule had is gone.
findings.failure: period Windows(100) evaluated per flush over 20,000 windows: at batch_windows=64, 87 of 198 gaps are shorter than 100 (min 64, gaps alternate 128/64); at batch_windows=8, 99 of 198 (min 96). At the tree's own cited longrun config CKPT_EVERY=4000 / BATCH_W=12, 2 of 3 gaps are short (3996 vs 4000).

findings.claim: The `if int(period) <= 0: return False` early return sits ABOVE the clock.step kind check, so with a non-positive period due() never looks at `clock` at all.
findings.failure: Cadences({'g': Windows(0)}).due('g', Windows(0), None) returns False; the same call with 'garbage' as the clock also returns False; with Windows(100) it raises AttributeError. 'ckpt' is Windows(0) at the shipped defaults, so that one call site's clock argument is unvalidated while the other five gates still raise UnitError on a wrong-kind clock.

findings.claim: The new comment's run length is off by one: it says 'a checkpoint 632 times in a 633-window run'; compose(environ={}) reports run_windows = 634 windows and windows_in_epoch = 634, where the pre-fix rule fires 633 times.
findings.failure: pre-fix update rule driven on the real save_period(Windows(0)): 633-window run -> 632 fires; 634-window run -> 633 fires. compose(environ={}) hands cadence_audit run_windows=Windows(634).

checked_and_sound: END-TO-END on the real composed System (sysm.cadences / sysm.clock from compose(environ={}), 634 windows, A rows per window and the ckpt gate at the flush tail): ledger reads ckpt=(634 checks, 0 fires, None, Windows(0)), curve=(0,0,None,Windows(2000)), dom.manage=(634,6,Windows(601),Windows(100)), dom.rekey=(634,3,...,Windows(200)), fab.manage=(634,1,Windows(501),Windows(500)), progress=(634,6,...,Windows(100)).
NON-POSITIVE PERIOD IS NOW DISARMED: Windows(0) and Windows(-5) fire 0 times over 634 windows and the ledger reads (634, 0, None, Windows(0)) -- checks counted, fires zero, disarmed AND reached.

MODULO PATHOLOGY GONE: period Windows(2000) over 200,000 windows fires 99 times at EVERY batch_windows in {1,2,8,15,16,32}; the old flush-tail `(step-1) % 2000 == 0` form fires 0 times at every batch_windows > 1 in the same loop.
RATE IS NOW PHASE-INDEPENDENT: per-window and per-flush fire counts are IDENTICAL for every (period, batch_windows) in {100,200,500,2000} x {1,2,8,15,16,32,64} over 200,000 windows.
THE FOUR NUMBERS THE NEW COMMENT CITES REPRODUCE EXACTLY: pre-fix effective period over 20,000 windows at declared 100 = 100.5 (B=1), 104.2 (B=8), 128.2 (B=32), 129.0 (B=64).
LEDGER THIRD STATE WORKS: a declared-but-never-evaluated key is PRESENT as (0, 0, None, period); an undeclared key raises KeyError and never enters the ledger.
LAZY SEED == RESUMED STEP: resume_step=5000 first-fires at 5101, resume_step=0 first-fires at 101 -- the same offset, which is exactly what ':5281-5282 seeds at the RESUMED step' asks for.
NO LEGITIMATE CALLER TRIPS THE PERIOD-DISAGREEMENT REFUSAL: the LOOP_ORDER call form re-invokes the accessor at every evaluation; 5000 windows x 5 accessors = 25,000 fresh period objects, 0 raises.

KIND GUARDS HOLD: bare int, float, None and Flushes all raise at both new_cadences (build time) and due(); a Windows SUBCLASS cannot even be declared (units.__init_subclass__ refuses a kind outside CLOCK_KINDS).
NO DOUBLE FIRE AND NO SUB-PERIOD GAP UNDER CONTINUOUS PER-WINDOW EVALUATION: gaps are exactly the period at P in {1,7,100,2000} over 200,000 windows.
could_not_break: asking one key twice in one window: the first call consumes the event and the second returns False -- matches compose.py's stated expectation
new_cadences build-time type guard catches every wrong kind I could pass
the catch-up burst is bounded at exactly one short gap per blackout, not an unbounded run of fires

I could NOT name a live call site in ASSEMBLY_ORDER/LOOP_ORDER that produces an evaluation blackout long enough to trigger the catch-up burst; the R8 finding is a property of the primitive's stated contract, demonstrated by a constructed blackout, not an observed run.
